summary: Migration smoke test — MarketScanner (Hrishi Associates). Wiring is mostly correct: ingress → uvicorn shim (:8001) → Node Express (:8055) works end-to-end for GET/POST/JSON/cookies. Frontend loads, admin login (HrishiAdmin@2026) succeeds, dashboard renders with 'Hrishi Associates' brand and full 9-item top nav, KITE LIVE DATA OFFLINE banner shows as expected, and 4 major pages (Home, Derivatives→Option Chain, Portfolio Analyser, Admin Console) render post-login without blank/error-boundary states. BUT — a CRITICAL security bug was discovered in the reverse-proxy shim /app/backend/server.py: it uses a shared httpx.AsyncClient whose cookie jar accumulates Set-Cookie from every upstream response and replays those cookies on every subsequent request from any user. Once ONE admin logs in via the /api proxy, every anonymous visitor thereafter is treated as an authenticated owner — effectively bypassing the entire auth gate for the whole preview environment.

critical.issue: Shared httpx.AsyncClient cookie jar leaks session cookies across ALL clients — after any admin login, anonymous requests via the ingress get 'authenticated:true' from /api/auth/status and bypass all owner-gated endpoints. Reproduced deterministically: (1) restart uvicorn → anonymous /api/auth/status returns authenticated:false; (2) POST /api/auth/login with correct password → 200 {ok:true}; (3) another curl -b '' /api/auth/status (no cookies) → authenticated:true. Direct call to Node on :8055 correctly returns authenticated:false, confirming the leak is inside the FastAPI shim. Root cause: httpx.AsyncClient stores cookies in `self._cookies` by default, and build_request()/send() persist/replay them. Fix: pass `cookies=None` or `cookie_jar=httpx.Cookies()` per request, or set `client.cookies = httpx.Cookies()` after every response; simplest — don't reuse a client with implicit jar (use client.stream with explicit cookies argument or construct httpx.AsyncClient(cookies=httpx.Cookies()) per request).

integration_issues.issue: When the Node api-server hits its 300 req/min ratelimit and returns 429 for boot-time API calls, some deep-linked routes render an empty <body> instead of the app shell. In-app SPA navigation (clicking nav anchors) works correctly — Portfolio, Admin Console, and Option Chain all rendered with real content post-login. Not a functional bug for a real user; possibly worth resilience-hardening for the boot path so a 429 storm doesn't blank the shell. Not blocking migration.

action_items: URGENT — fix proxy cookie-jar leak in /app/backend/server.py: create a per-request httpx.Cookies() or set client.cookies = httpx.Cookies() so the shim doesn't accumulate/replay Set-Cookie across users. This is a full-tenant auth bypass for the preview URL.
Optional: harden the SPA boot path so an initial burst of 429s (auth/status, kite/status, indices, etc.) doesn't leave the shell blank on hard refresh of a deep link.

Per-request httpx.AsyncClient() (or explicit cookies=jar_per_call) is the standard fix. This is the highest-priority issue.

rca of the issue: PROXY COOKIE LEAK — Reproduction: `sudo supervisorctl restart backend && sleep 3 && curl https://.../api/auth/status` → returns authenticated:false. Now `curl -X POST .../api/auth/login -d '{"password":"HrishiAdmin@2026"}' -H 'content-type: application/json'` → {ok:true}. Now `curl https://.../api/auth/status` from a DIFFERENT client (no cookies, no session) → returns authenticated:true. Compare with `curl http://127.0.0.1:8055/api/auth/status` (bypasses shim, hits Node directly) → correctly returns authenticated:false. Root cause: httpx.AsyncClient in /app/backend/server.py line 13 is instantiated once at process start with default cookies=httpx.Cookies(). Every response's Set-Cookie header populates that shared jar, and every subsequent client.send() replays those cookies to the upstream Node server. When the Node server sees its own valid signed 'scanner_session' cookie it (correctly) returns authenticated=true. Mitigation: change proxy to build cookies explicitly per-request from request.headers['cookie'] only and pass extensions={'cookies': httpx.Cookies()} — or drop the shared client and use `async with httpx.AsyncClient() as c:` per request. The Node code itself is fine — this is 100% a shim-layer bug introduced during the Emergent migration.
